title: Back in Lansing: father's job at Bell Telephone and settling down
summary: Return to Lansing, his father's work as one of the first Black employees of Bell Telephone, and things settling down at school.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: So let's see, that was a year in Charleston and then it was back to Jackson, Michigan, or to Lansing?

It was to Lansing and my father had rented a house and my mohter and they were supposed to get together again and they were together for a little while, then when--you know--she disappeared--you know--with the car and everything. When I came home from school the next day, that's when he had the player piano and was playin'. I look back on that, it was marvelous, for a man to have that kind of brain, so he didn't want me to come home sad, you dig what I mean. So I'll never forget that.
Now, what work did your father do?

He was one of the first colored men to be employed by the Bell Telephone System in Jackson, Michigan. He stayed there until he died. Yeah, one of the first employees of the Bell Telephone Company and I got pictures of him in 1927--like that--with all these employees in Jackson, Michigan.
And he never remarried as well?
Oh no, no, no, no. Uhuh.
Now had you gone to school at all before you came back there to Lansing? Had you gone to school in St. Louis?
Yeah, I went to school in St. Louis, I remember that, but everything was so jimble-jamble, I don't even know when I was in school or when I was out.
But when you got back to Lansing, then things settled down a little bit?
